**Coordinates:** Recognition · in its own seat · Unacknowledged

**Self-seat rule:** Recognition applied to its own domain — what Recognition does is call things by their right name, register what has arrived, confirm that something real has happened. In its own seat, it applies that function to itself: it would need to recognize its own recognizing. Unacknowledged status means this self-application isn't happening.

**What Recognition does:** It completes a loop — something happens, Recognition fires, the thing is registered as real and done. Without that firing, things remain in an ambiguous state: happened but not confirmed.

**Unacknowledged (status vocabulary reserved — can't say "unacknowledged" in prose):** The signature isn't doing its work. The tax on the surrounding structure: things that need confirming pile up unconfirmed. The loop stays open.

**Self-seat + status:** Recognition can't register itself. So it can't know when *it* has fired, when *it* has confirmed something. Every act of recognizing stays in question. The machine that closes loops cannot close its own loop — so nothing ever fully lands.

**Draft core:**
Recognition closes the loop: something happens, Recognition names it, and it becomes real and done. In its own seat, the thing being named is the act of naming itself — whether the registering has actually registered. Without that closing, Recognition keeps firing without landing: confirmations that never confirm themselves, loops that stay open, and nothing fully counts as finished.

Without that, confirmations don't land. Loops stay open. Nothing fully counts as finished, because the thing that would count it is the one still waiting to be counted.
